metric: Callgrind retired instructions (Ir), exact integers, no interval (AGENTS.md 8.4)
question: where the single-threaded cost of sharded allocator accounting sits, and which layout removes it

provenance.host: development box, 72-core x86_64 (NOT the reference host; no bench lock taken)
provenance.source: git archive 686dd6cb into a scratch tree; the repository's tracked files were not modified
provenance.per_cell_target_dirs: used throughout, per the Cargo metadata-hash trap found in the fifth cell
provenance.reference: c5base2, built and measured in the SAME batch as c6
provenance.reference_arm: each cell is compared against a base built in the SAME batch
provenance.not_the_reference_host: measured on a development box; no bench lock was taken and no wall-clock claim is made from this artifact

build_reproducibility.test: c5base vs c5base2: two independent builds of the identical extracted tree
build_reproducibility.verdict: the build is NOT bit-reproducible for these three *_short string arms; 126/129 are. Any delta on them below ~3,000 Ir is build noise. The other 126 arms are exactly reproducible.

noise_floor.measured: two builds of the identical tree differ by up to 2,800 Ir on these three; any delta on them below that is build noise, not a code effect

cells.c5a: size-only dummy array, no writer_slot() (4864 B / align 64)
cells.c5b: sharded with the array boxed out of line (696 B / align 8)
cells.c6: deferred-gated lazy shards behind OnceLock<Box<..>> (728 B / align 8)
cells.c7: deferred-gated lazy shards behind AtomicPtr, Release/Acquire (720 B / align 8)

aggregate_ir_delta.verdict: on the sync_* aggregate c6 (+21,139,666) and c7 (+21,202,797) are indistinguishable — a 0.3% difference. The Once-state load was NOT the cost. Both remain ~4x inline sharding's sync cost (+5,362,207). c7 also gives back c6's negative non-sync aggregate (-839,838 -> +805,426).

gate_decomposition.reference: c5base4, pristine 686dd6cb built in the same batch
gate_decomposition.prediction: c8 sync aggregate near sharded (+5 to +8 M)
gate_decomposition.falsifier: c8 at +18 M or worse => the cost is the GATE, not the indirection
gate_decomposition.outcome: REFUTED. c8 = +17.63 M, at the falsifier and 2.2x the top of the predicted band. The gate costs +12.27 M; the indirection costs +3.51 M. The gate is 3.5x the indirection.
gate_decomposition.c9_finding: c9 does NOT take both wins. At 1,024 B of shards it still perturbs the read arms by +2.188% (vs 4,096 B's +2.191%) and its sync aggregate is WORSE than c8's. The read-arm perturbation is therefore not proportional to the array's size — 1 KiB perturbs as much as 4 KiB — which points at the alignment change to 64 and the field-offset shift, not the magnitude.

winner.why: the only cell with bit-identical read arms (0 Ir), the best non-sync aggregate (-838,766), the fewest rows over 0.5% (17) and the lowest worst case (+2.449%). c8 and c9 both reinstate the plain-arm cost and neither recovers the sync aggregate.
winner.caveat: the sync-arm cost is dominated by the GATE, which c6/c8/c9 all share, so the wall-clock question is about the gate. Hoisting the deferred check out of the per-allocation path is the indicated fix and is NOT in this patch.
